raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-IND-ChhattisgarhAcceleratedLearning",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Extreme weather (droughts/floods) may force extensions of school summer breaks, reducing instructional days and delaying learning outcomes.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate buffer days in academic calendar, develop remote learning modules, and establish climate‑resilient school schedules.",
      "evidence": "Section B.3: state is vulnerable to droughts and floods ... can force extensions of the annual school summer break and reduce the number of days for instruction."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Insufficient in‑service teacher training and shortage of subject‑specialist teachers could limit improvements in learning quality.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Roll out the structured TaRL multi‑year training, monitor completion rates, and recruit additional subject teachers with merit‑based hiring.",
      "evidence": "Section 11: majority of teachers lack access to adequate in‑service training ... lack of subject teachers ... limited in‑service training support is resulting in poor quality of teaching‑learning interactions."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Over 84% of the education budget is spent on salaries, limiting funds for quality improvements and infrastructure upgrades.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Leverage results‑based financing to free up savings, prioritize expenditures in the PDO, and seek additional counterpart funding.",
      "evidence": "Section 18: 84.8 percent of the consolidated budget ... is used to pay salaries ... This limits the funds available for improving the quality of education and for investments in strengthening the network of schools."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Weak procurement planning and lack of annual procurement plans may cause delays in civil works for model schools.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate preparation of annual procurement plans, train staff on e‑GP usage, and monitor timelines through the STEP system.",
      "evidence": "Section 61‑64: procurement governed by FMP Manual but \"no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan\" and reliance on e‑GP platform."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Limited institutional capacity for environmental and social (E&S) management may lead to non‑compliance with fire safety, waste and accessibility standards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct E&S capacity‑building workshops, embed fire‑safety and waste‑management clauses in contracts, and establish a dedicated E&S officer.",
      "evidence": "Section 70: weak institutional capacity for E&S activity implementation, gap in fire safety norms, lack of provisions for universal access, etc."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Inadequate data protection for the EMIS and digital assessments could result in privacy breaches or loss of student records.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt robust data‑protection policies, encrypt EMIS databases, and conduct periodic privacy impact assessments aligned with national legislation.",
      "evidence": "Legal Covenants (Section IV): activities involving collection, storage, usage, and/or processing of Personal Data must be carried out with due regard to legal framework."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Delayed or incomplete verification of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) may postpone fund releases and affect implementation timelines.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Ensure timely appointment of Independent Verification Agency, set clear verification schedules, and use the EMIS dashboard for real‑time DLI tracking.",
      "evidence": "Section V: funds will be disbursed on achievement of DLRs verified by an IVA; verification protocols outlined in Annex 2."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Social norms and topographic barriers may limit boys' enrollment in senior secondary science and commerce streams.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide residential facilities for boys, conduct community outreach, and align school placement with local needs to encourage enrollment.",
      "evidence": "Section 6: families prefer boys to work; topographic challenges in accessing senior secondary schools; residential schools not available for adolescent boys."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Substantial fiduciary risk due to multiple implementing agencies and weak internal controls could lead to misallocation of funds.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen internal audit, enforce anti‑corruption guidelines, and implement a risk‑based audit plan with an audit committee oversight.",
      "evidence": "Section 56‑57: IFSA concludes fiduciary risk is ‘Substantial’; systemic gaps observed in implementation; need for strengthening internal controls."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Technical support agencies engaged under IPF‑TA may lack capacity or continuity, reducing effectiveness of training and EMIS development.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Define clear TORs, include deliverable milestones, monitor performance quarterly, and ensure knowledge transfer to state institutions.",
      "evidence": "Section 4.1: IPF‑TA will engage technical experts; Section 4.5 notes constraints of agencies such as limited funding and scalability."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Climate change could damage school infrastructure, compromising safety and continuity of education.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate disaster‑resilient designs, use energy‑ and water‑efficient fixtures, and conduct periodic climate‑risk assessments for school sites.",
      "evidence": "Section 34‑35: RA‑3 will support climate‑proofing school infrastructure with disaster‑resilient designs and energy‑efficient fixtures."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Gender‑based violence and safety concerns may deter attendance, especially for girls, affecting enrollment targets.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement SRGBV training for principals, establish a robust grievance redress mechanism, and conduct regular safety audits.",
      "evidence": "Section 74‑75: training on SRGBV for school leaders; GRM strengthening; alignment with best practices for SEA/SH."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Multi‑tier budgeting and late approval of Annual Work Plans may cause cash‑flow gaps and slow project execution.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Accelerate AWP&B submission, secure provisional releases, and monitor fund flow through the Single Nodal Account dashboard.",
      "evidence": "Section 59‑60: AWP&B approved only by the third to fifth month of the financial year, leading to delays in fund releases."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Insufficient integration of climate education into curricula may limit achievement of climate‑adaptation outcomes.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Embed climate competencies in learning standards, develop dedicated lesson plans, and include climate items in diagnostic assessments.",
      "evidence": "Section 25 & 28: RA‑1 and RA‑2 focus on integrating climate change education into teacher training and assessments."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities in schools could affect student health and attendance.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Include WASH standards in school design, monitor toilet and drinking‑water functionality, and allocate budget for regular maintenance.",
      "evidence": "Section 70: lack of provisions for drinking water facilities, toilets, and maintenance leading to service disruption."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Extreme weather (droughts/floods) may force extensions of school summer breaks, reducing instructional days and delaying learning outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Integrate buffer days in academic calendar, develop remote learning modules, and establish climate‑resilient school schedules.
risks.evidence: Section B.3: state is vulnerable to droughts and floods ... can force extensions of the annual school summer break and reduce the number of days for instruction.

risks.description: Insufficient in‑service teacher training and shortage of subject‑specialist teachers could limit improvements in learning quality.
risks.mitigation: Roll out the structured TaRL multi‑year training, monitor completion rates, and recruit additional subject teachers with merit‑based hiring.
risks.evidence: Section 11: majority of teachers lack access to adequate in‑service training ... lack of subject teachers ... limited in‑service training support is resulting in poor quality of teaching‑learning interactions.

risks.description: Over 84% of the education budget is spent on salaries, limiting funds for quality improvements and infrastructure upgrades.
risks.mitigation: Leverage results‑based financing to free up savings, prioritize expenditures in the PDO, and seek additional counterpart funding.
risks.evidence: Section 18: 84.8 percent of the consolidated budget ... is used to pay salaries ... This limits the funds available for improving the quality of education and for investments in strengthening the network of schools.

risks.description: Weak procurement planning and lack of annual procurement plans may cause delays in civil works for model schools.
risks.mitigation: Mandate preparation of annual procurement plans, train staff on e‑GP usage, and monitor timelines through the STEP system.
risks.evidence: Section 61‑64: procurement governed by FMP Manual but "no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan" and reliance on e‑GP platform.

risks.description: Limited institutional capacity for environmental and social (E&S) management may lead to non‑compliance with fire safety, waste and accessibility standards.
risks.mitigation: Conduct E&S capacity‑building workshops, embed fire‑safety and waste‑management clauses in contracts, and establish a dedicated E&S officer.
risks.evidence: Section 70: weak institutional capacity for E&S activity implementation, gap in fire safety norms, lack of provisions for universal access, etc.

risks.description: Inadequate data protection for the EMIS and digital assessments could result in privacy breaches or loss of student records.
risks.mitigation: Adopt robust data‑protection policies, encrypt EMIS databases, and conduct periodic privacy impact assessments aligned with national legislation.
risks.evidence: Legal Covenants (Section IV): activities involving collection, storage, usage, and/or processing of Personal Data must be carried out with due regard to legal framework.

risks.description: Delayed or incomplete verification of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) may postpone fund releases and affect implementation timelines.
risks.mitigation: Ensure timely appointment of Independent Verification Agency, set clear verification schedules, and use the EMIS dashboard for real‑time DLI tracking.
risks.evidence: Section V: funds will be disbursed on achievement of DLRs verified by an IVA; verification protocols outlined in Annex 2.

risks.description: Social norms and topographic barriers may limit boys' enrollment in senior secondary science and commerce streams.
risks.mitigation: Provide residential facilities for boys, conduct community outreach, and align school placement with local needs to encourage enrollment.
risks.evidence: Section 6: families prefer boys to work; topographic challenges in accessing senior secondary schools; residential schools not available for adolescent boys.

risks.description: Substantial fiduciary risk due to multiple implementing agencies and weak internal controls could lead to misallocation of funds.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen internal audit, enforce anti‑corruption guidelines, and implement a risk‑based audit plan with an audit committee oversight.
risks.evidence: Section 56‑57: IFSA concludes fiduciary risk is ‘Substantial’; systemic gaps observed in implementation; need for strengthening internal controls.

risks.description: Technical support agencies engaged under IPF‑TA may lack capacity or continuity, reducing effectiveness of training and EMIS development.
risks.mitigation: Define clear TORs, include deliverable milestones, monitor performance quarterly, and ensure knowledge transfer to state institutions.
risks.evidence: Section 4.1: IPF‑TA will engage technical experts; Section 4.5 notes constraints of agencies such as limited funding and scalability.

risks.description: Climate change could damage school infrastructure, compromising safety and continuity of education.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate disaster‑resilient designs, use energy‑ and water‑efficient fixtures, and conduct periodic climate‑risk assessments for school sites.
risks.evidence: Section 34‑35: RA‑3 will support climate‑proofing school infrastructure with disaster‑resilient designs and energy‑efficient fixtures.

risks.description: Gender‑based violence and safety concerns may deter attendance, especially for girls, affecting enrollment targets.
risks.mitigation: Implement SRGBV training for principals, establish a robust grievance redress mechanism, and conduct regular safety audits.
risks.evidence: Section 74‑75: training on SRGBV for school leaders; GRM strengthening; alignment with best practices for SEA/SH.

risks.description: Multi‑tier budgeting and late approval of Annual Work Plans may cause cash‑flow gaps and slow project execution.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate AWP&B submission, secure provisional releases, and monitor fund flow through the Single Nodal Account dashboard.
risks.evidence: Section 59‑60: AWP&B approved only by the third to fifth month of the financial year, leading to delays in fund releases.

risks.description: Insufficient integration of climate education into curricula may limit achievement of climate‑adaptation outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Embed climate competencies in learning standards, develop dedicated lesson plans, and include climate items in diagnostic assessments.
risks.evidence: Section 25 & 28: RA‑1 and RA‑2 focus on integrating climate change education into teacher training and assessments.

risks.description: Inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities in schools could affect student health and attendance.
risks.mitigation: Include WASH standards in school design, monitor toilet and drinking‑water functionality, and allocate budget for regular maintenance.
risks.evidence: Section 70: lack of provisions for drinking water facilities, toilets, and maintenance leading to service disruption.
